pr_body:
There was a problem with the error handling in AES wrap which fell back to a default _final error_.  This adds a fix for the error and more specific errors for the different failure possibilities.
    
Fixes #16387

- [ ] documentation is added or updated
- [ ] tests are added or updated

issue_context.title: EVP_Cipher does not correctly return errors
issue_context.body:
OpenSSL version: 3.0.0-beta2

The `EVP_Cipher` function does not correctly return errors in some cases, but `EVP_CipherUpdate` and `EVP_CipherFinal_ex` do. This was mainly tested for the AES KeyWrap mode, but might also be present in other modes.

The [`aes_wrap_cipher`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/providers/implementations/ciphers/cipher_aes_wrp.c#L198) function in `cipher_aes_wrp.c` calls [`aes_wrap_cipher_internal`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/providers/implementations/ciphers/cipher_aes_wrp.c#L142), in the same file, which returns -1 if an error occurred, or the output length otherwise. For some reason, the `aes_wrap_cipher` function takes this value and compares it with 0. If the value is 0, it returns -1.

As a result, when an error occurs in `aes_wrap_cipher_internal`, the return value of `aes_wrap_cipher` will actually be 1, and the `outl` variable will be set to -1. This strange behaviour is handled correctly, albeit in a roundabout way, by `EVP_CipherUpdate` and `EVP_CipherFinal_ex`:
* [`EVP_EncryptUpdate`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/evp/evp_enc.c#L633), part of `EVP_CipherUpdate`
* [`EVP_EncryptFinal_ex`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/evp/evp_enc.c#L693), part of `EVP_CipherFinal_ex`
* [`EVP_DecryptUpdate`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/evp/evp_enc.c#L780), part of `EVP_CipherUpdate`
* [`EVP_DecryptFinal_ex`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/evp/evp_enc.c#L915), part of `EVP_CipherFinal_ex`

Notice the check in these functions, something like:
```c
    if (ret) {
        if (soutl > INT_MAX) {
            ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_EVP, EVP_R_FINAL_ERROR);
            return 0;
        }
        *outl = soutl;
    }
```

This check is absent in the [`EVP_Cipher`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/evp/evp_lib.c#L403) function, and the function simply passes the return value of 1, with the value of `outl` ignored.

The [poc.txt](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/files/7032797/poc.txt) file contains proof-of-concept code to test this bug. Two ciphertexts are decrypted using AES-KW, one with a correct IV, and one with an incorrect IV.

When `USE_EVP_CIPHER` is set to 1, the following output is shown:
```
OpenSSL 3.0.0-beta2 29 Jul 2021
Plaintext: 03010401050902060503050809070903
Plaintext: 00000000000000000000000000000000
```
Notice that no error is thrown, instead an all-zero plaintext is returned. The caller cannot distinguish between a valid, all-zero plaintext, and an incorrect IV.

When `USE_EVP_CIPHER` is set to 0, it shows the expected output:
```
OpenSSL 3.0.0-beta2 29 Jul 2021
Plaintext: 03010401050902060503050809070903
807B5E0DC57F0000:error:030000BD:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptUpdate:update error:crypto/evp/evp_enc.c:781:
```

review_comments: Should this be `len < 0` or just `len == -1`? I would argue 0 is a valid return value from `aes_wrap_cipher_internal`, as it means the input/output is empty.

What about: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/ed3f51ec7d2f8956bff7bedf99b65ff1595e02e8/providers/implementations/ciphers/cipher_aes_wrp.c#L150-L152

Should `aes_wrap_cipher` return an error in that case?
